parts.text: A student determines the focal length of a converging lens by two methods. Fig. 3.1

ms.label: 3(a)
ms.text:
one precaution from:
(lamp), object and lens at same height /
lens and screen perpendicular(to bench) /
fix metre rule to bench

parts.label: b
parts.text: (b) The student sets the distance u between the illuminated object and the lens to 20.0 cm. He places the screen near the lens and moves the screen until a sharp image of the illuminated object is seen on the screen.

ms.label: 3(b)(i)
ms.text: move screen slowly / back and forth

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Measure v 1 , the distance from the lens to the screen on Fig. 3.1. v 1 = ........................................................ cm Fig. 3.1 is drawn to 1/10th scale. Calculate V 1 , the actual distance from the lens to the screen. V 1 = ........................................................ cm [2]

parts.label: c
parts.text: (c) The shapes of the illuminated object and the image seen on the screen are shown full size in Fig. 3.2 and Fig. 3.3. Fig. 3.2 Fig. 3.3

parts.label: i
parts.text: (i) Measure h O , the height of the illuminated object, as shown in Fig. 3.2. h O = ........................................................ cm Measure h I , the height of the image on the screen, as shown in Fig. 3.3. h I = ........................................................ cm [1]

parts.label: ii
parts.text: (ii) Calculate a value M for the magnification, using the equation M = h I h O . M = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(c)(ii)
ms.text: correct calculation of M (4.0 / ecf) and no unit

parts.label: d
parts.text: (d) Calculate a value f 1 for the focal length of the lens. Use your values from (b)(ii) and (c)(ii) and the equation f 1 = V 1 ( M + 1) . f 1 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(e)
ms.text:
any one valid difficulty (e.g. hand or ruler gets in way of light)
one improvement to overcome the difficulty (e.g. translucent screen (and measure from back) / fix grid to screen)

parts.label: f
parts.text: (f) The student adjusts the position of the lens so that u = 40.0 cm and obtains a new value V 2 for the distance between the lens and the screen. 25.1 V 2 = ........................................................ cm Calculate a second value f 2 for the focal length of the lens, using the equation f 2 = uV 2 ( u + V 2 ) . f 2 = ......................................................... [1]

ms.label: 3(f)
ms.text: f2 = 15.4 and cm seen at least once in (d) or (f) and not contradicted

ms.label: 3(g)
ms.text:
valid suggestion with reason
e.g: f2 as f1 has smaller measurements (i.e. ho and hi) (and so % uncertainties larger)
